Mursid @ Bablu vs Rajesh Ohri on 25 February, 2020 1 In The Court Of Ms. Hemani Malhotra, Judge Motor Vehicle Accident Claim Tribunal02, West District, Tis Hazari Courts, Delhi Petition No.76478/2016 Fir No.435/13 Ps Janak Puri Mohd. Mursid @ Bablu S/o Abdul Kashus, R/o Village Pari Paran Pat, Khusmode Ps Bargame, District Araria, Bihar (Injured) ......Petition Versus 1. Rajesh Ohri S/o Rajender Kumar Ohri R/o B1/473, First Floor, Janakpuri, New Delhi (DrivercumOwner) 2. United India Insurance Company Ltd. At: 2 Lsc Okhla PhaseII, near C Lal Chowk, New Delhi (Insurer) ..... Respondents Date of Institution : 15.12.2014 Date of conclusion of arguments : 17.02.2020 Date of pronouncement of judgment/award : 25.02.2020 Award 1.
texts.facts: This judgmentcumaward shall decide the claim of petitioner Mohd. Mursid filed under Sections 166 and 140 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred to as "M.V. Act") as amended up to date to claim compensation for the injuries sustained by him in a road vehicular accident that took place on 14.11.2013. FIR No.435/13 u/ss 279/337 IPC was registered at Police Station Janak Puri and chargesheet was filed against respondent No.1/Rajesh Ohri, drivercumowner of Car bearing registration No.DL7CN1867 (offending vehicle). 2 2. Detailed Accident Report (DAR) was filed by the Investigating Officer (IO) along with copies of the criminal proceedings including FIR and chargesheet. Mohd. Mursid @ Bablu vs Rajesh Ohri on 25 February, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/44431814/ 1 3. Brief facts of the vehicular accident as averred in the claim petition as well as DAR are that at about 07:00 PM on 14.11.2013, petitioner/injured Mohd.Mursid was going on his scooty bearing registration No.PB10DV9185. When he reached near B1, Super Bazar road, Janak Puri, the offending vehicle came at a high speed in a rash and negligent manner and after overtaking scooty of the petitioner, took a sharp right turn. During the said process, the scooty of the petitioner and offending vehicle collided with each other. Resultantly, petitioner sustained grievous injuries. Thereafter, he was removed to DDU Hospital for treatment. 4. Subsequently, it transpired that the offending vehicle was owned and driven by respondent No.1/Rajesh Ohri and insured with respondent No.2/United India Insurance Company Ltd. 5. In the Written Statement filed on behalf of respondent No.1, it was averred that the accident was caused due to sole negligence of petitioner as he was a minor and driving two wheeler without any driving licence. It was further averred that it is evident from the site plan as well as Mechanical Inspection Report of the car that alleged offending vehicle was struck on the left side, meaning thereby, that injured/petitioner had struck his scooty against the car while the car had come forward to cross the road. It was stated that since the alleged offending vehicle was duly insured with respondent No.2/insurance company, hence, no liability could be fastened upon respondent No.1. 6. In the Written Statement filed on behalf of respondent No.2/insurance company, it was admitted that the alleged offending vehicle was insured with respondent No.2 vide its Policy bearing No.0406033112P014972 valid from 31.12.2020 to 30.12.2013. 7. From the pleadings of the parties, contentions raised and material on record, the following issues were framed by the Learned Predecessor of this Tribunal vide order dated 09.03.2015: ISSUES: 1. In a claim petition filed under u/s 166/140 of the M.V. Act, onus is on the claimant(s)/petitioner(s) to prove that he or she sustained injuries in a vehicular Mohd. Mursid @ Bablu vs Rajesh Ohri on 25 February, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/44431814/ 2 accident caused by the wrongful act or negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle. 11. In support of his claim, petitioner examined Dr.Perminder Kaur, CMO(SAG), GGSG Hospital as PW1; ASI Narender Kumar, IO as PW2; Ghyanshyam Lal, Senior Executive Medical Record, Kalra Hospital as PW3; Amit Sharma, MRD Incharge, Orchid Hospital as PW4; Sachin Kumar, Partner of Ananya International as PW5 (inadvertently mentioned as PW4). PECUNIARY DAMAGES (Special Damages) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization and medicines 19.
texts.arguments: It was thus, very vehemently argued by learned counsel for the insurance company that the petitioner had failed to prove negligence of the offending vehicle. It was also urged that in such circumstances, the outcome of issue No.1 would hinge upon the testimony of respondent No.1/drivercumowner of the offending vehicle. 13. Per contra, it was contended by learned counsel for petitioner that even though petitioner did not step in the witness box, the negligence of respondent No.1 in causing the accident was proved by testimony of PW2/ASI Narendra Kumar, who had recorded the statement of petitioner on 30.10.2014 and had proved the 4 same as Ex.PW2/R1/1, wherein, the petitioner had imputed negligence of the offending vehicle in the accident in question. 14. The argument of learned counsel for petitioner does not hold any water as it is difficult to believe that any statement (Ex.PW2/R1/1) was given by the petitioner to PW2/ASI Narendra Kumar. The medical treatment record of petitioner Mohd. Murshid reflects that he had sustained severe head injury with polytrauma, fracture right wrist joint. He was admitted to Kalra Hospital on 15.11.2013 and discharged on 28.11.2013 against Medical Advise. In RAJ KUMAR VS. AJAY KUMAR & ANOTHER (2011) 1 SCC 343, Hon'ble Supreme Court of India has laid down general principles for computation of compensation in injury cases. The relevant paras of the judgment are reproduced as under: 5. The provision of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 ("the Act", for short) makes clear that the award must be just, which means that compensation should, to the extent possible, fully and adequately restore the claimant to the position prior to the accident. The object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner. . A person is not only to be compensated for th physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury. 26. So far as, the monthly income of petitioner is concerned, the testimony of PW4/Sachin Kumar does not inspire confidence as he failed to produce any Mohd. Mursid @ Bablu vs Rajesh Ohri on 25 February, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/44431814/ 5 document for disbursement of salary to the petitioner. In the absence of any supportive document qua income of the injured/petitioner, he is considered as an Unskilled Worker as per Minimum Wage Rates prevailing in Delhi at the time of accident. Accordingly, income of the petitioner is assessed as Rs.8,086/ per month as on the date of accident. 27. In a judgment titled as JAGDISH VS. MOHAN AND OTHERS, reported as 2018 ACJ 1011 delivered by three Judges Bench of Hon'ble Supreme Court, the Hon'ble Supreme Court awarded compensation towards loss of future prospects in a case where the petitioner had sustained physical disability of 90% due to amputation of both his hands. 8 28. In view of the ratio in the aforecited case, it is imperative to calculate compensation towards loss of future prospects to ascertain compensation on account of loss of earning in the instant case. 29. Admittedly, petitioner was aged 20 years at the time of accident, hence, in view of the ratio of judgment titled as NATIONAL INSURANCE COMPANY VS. PRANAY SETHI & ORS. decided on 31.10.2017 by the Hon'ble Supreme Court , an addition of 40% of Rs.8,086/ (Rs.3,234.40 p.m.) is made towards future prospects in the income of the petitioner/injured. Thus, total monthly income of the petitioner after making an addition of future prospects would be Rs.11,320.40 per month. Since petitioner was aged 20 years at the time of the accident, hence, applying the criteria of multiplier laid down in SARLA VERMA AND OTHERS VS. DELHI TRANSPORT CORPORATION AND ANOTHER, (2009) 6 SUPREME COURT CASES 121, the multiplier applicable in this case would be 18 (eighteen). 32. In R.D. HATTANGADI VS. PEST CONTROL (INDIA) PVT.LTD., I (1995) ACC 281 (SC), where a road accident resulted in 100% disability due to paraplegia below waist to a lawyer (retired Judge), the Supreme Court observed as under: "That no amount of compensation can restore the physical frame of the appellant. That is why it has been said by Courts that whenever any Mohd. Mursid @ Bablu vs Rajesh Ohri on 25 February, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/44431814/ 6 amount is determined as the compensation payable for any injury suffered during an accident, the object is to compensate such injured "so far as money can compensate" because it is impossible to equate the money with the human sufferings or personal deprivations. Money cannot renew a broken and shattered physical frame. 36. In JAGDISH VS. MOHAN (Supra), it was further observed as under: "11. Our yardsticks of compensation should not be so abysmal as to lead one to question whether our law values human life. Awards of compensation are not law's doles. In the case of Mohd. Mursid @ Bablu vs Rajesh Ohri on 25 February, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/44431814/ 8 50. In order to avoid the compensation money being frittered away, balance amount of Rs.31,00,000/ (Rupees Thirty One Lakh) would be kept in FDRs in accordance with the order dt. 07.12.2018 passed by Hon'ble Mr.Justice J.R. Midha in RAJESH TYAGI & ORS. VS. JAIBIR SINGH & ORS. IN FAO NO.842/2003 as per details mentioned herein: "An Amount of Rs.31,00,000/ be kept in 310 (three hundred ten) fixed deposits of Rs.10,000/ (Rupees Ten Thousand) each, in the name of petitioner for the period of one month to 310 months respectively, with cumulative interest; However, money can be withdrawn through withdrawal slip only. 51. (f) The concerned bank shall not issue any cheque book and/or debit card to claimant(s).
